history.title: M0 — Scaffold and guardrails
history.intro: The project started from a build kit: the game design, architecture, art bible and build plan, written before any code.
bullets: Phaser 4 (pinned), TypeScript in strict mode, Vite, Zod for content, Vitest and Playwright for tests, ESLint and Prettier.
The ground rule: the game’s rules ("the sim") are pure, deterministic code that never touches the screen, so every hunt can be replayed exactly.
All tuning numbers live in JSON content files, checked by schemas.

history.title: M1 — Deterministic game engine
history.intro: A whole hunt ran without graphics: from a seed, the content and the player’s inputs to a result.
bullets: 60 ticks per second; named random streams so spawns, pellets and events never disturb each other.
Own sine, cosine and exponent maths, so every browser and phone computes the same numbers.
Scoring, guns, pellet spread, hit tests and replays; "golden" replays fail the tests if any rule changes by accident.

history.title: Training ground (Skietbaan)
history.intro: A shooting range on the admin page: try any gun, locked ones too, at any distance and see exactly how it shoots, without the pressure of a hunt.

Statistics per gun and distance: shots, hits, misses, hit %, shotgun pellets on target per shot; on paper, the last 20 holes are drawn with the group size (also as a % of a guineafowl’s width at that distance) and where the group centres against the aim. Reset and "Copy report".

history.title: v1.4 part B: the Namibië pack, camelthorn trees and the family nest, angry weavers
history.intro: A fifth hunting area, built for long range, and the first props drawn at the new, higher quality bar.
bullets: Camelthorn trees drawn in layers: furrowed bark lit and shaded on every limb, zig-zag branches, an umbrella crown of feathery clumps with sky between them, grey seed pods and dappled shade. The product owner approved them on 24 Oct.
The sociable weavers’ family nest: a domed haystack with over 2 000 straws, a hanging fringe and 10–20 entrance holes underneath. Branches pass through it and leaves grow over the top.

Angry weavers: shooting the nest costs 10 points and sends 6–15 small birds pouring out of the holes; they swirl, a few dart at the camera, and settle back after about 4 seconds. Their flight is worked out from the hunt itself, so replays show the same birds.

Namibië: the white Etosha salt pan, red Namib dunes, quiver trees, camelthorns and a waterhole flock far out on the pan. Every weekday map opens the farthest (Ver) plane; on Tuesdays, Thursdays and the bonus maps the far birds shimmer in a mirage.
It unlocks for good once Die Verste is reached in any area. The title screen gains an area picker that shows Namibië locked, with how to unlock it.

Balance: every gun and sight was measured over 200 hunts on all seven weekday maps and Saturday’s three bonus maps. A new per-plane points setting brought the scoped .22 (the strongest) under the 4 500 cap everywhere; its worst map is now 4 421.
First download still within the 3 MB budget; 1 027 unit tests.

history.title: Skietbaan gongs: clean steel plates with lasting hit marks
history.intro: The product owner asked for clean steel gongs on the training ground, with every shot visible for the whole session.
bullets: A freshly painted plate every visit: the fake "old hits" baked into the plate picture are gone. The plate has a clean bevelled steel rim and chains, and hangs from a timber frame with grain and bolts, drawn at double resolution so it stays sharp in the 3–9× scope.

Every hit leaves a lead-splash mark exactly where the bullet struck: a silver star with a dark centre and small flecks, sized by the gun. A shotgun pellet leaves a small mark, the .22 a medium one, and the Langloop and Kettie a large one. Each mark’s shape comes from the shot itself, so a replay draws the same marks.
Marks swing with the plate, and the newest one glints for a moment.

Steel and paper follow one rule: every mark and hole stays for the whole visit, through gun swaps, the scope and switching distances (paper used to show only the last 20). New buttons clear them on purpose: Repaint, New paper and Fresh targets.
Up to 400 marks per target are baked into one picture, so phones stay fast.
feedback: Product owner (24 Oct, 17:45): "The metal gongs need to be clean. And when shot, the shot should be visible and stay visible during the session. I want to see consistency."

The independent review found that the plate drawn before its picture loaded came out blank, a test that could not catch the bug it was meant for, marks shared between courses, and gun sizes written into the code instead of the gun data. Tank fixed all of them.

Claude’s screenshots showed no targets at all. A browser check found the cause in the tests rather than the game: the test mouse rested at the screen edge, which scrolls the view, so the shots went where the plate used to be. The tests now reload with a key and fail loudly if the view moves.

history.title: v1.5 Languages: text, voice and names for every audience
history.intro: The product owner wanted the game, the voice and the names in English, Afrikaans and German, so it works for more audiences.
bullets: Two separate settings: the text language (Auto, English, Afrikaans, German, Dutch) and the voice language (Same as text, English, Afrikaans, German). You can play with an Afrikaans voice and English subtitles. Dutch text uses the Afrikaans voice, the closest match.

Every name now has a proper English, German and Dutch version: guns, maps, the Gun Shed, the Notebook, the Bird Book, birds, secrets, charms, ranks and helpers. Dubbelloop becomes Double Barrel in English and Doppelflinte in German; Afrikaans keeps the farm names. Place names stay as they are.
An "Afrikaans names" switch keeps the Afrikaans flavour names in any language, for players who like them.

Oupa now speaks: his 43 comments and the short scolds are voiced in English, Afrikaans and German. The voices are interim, made offline with free, commercially usable text-to-speech (Kokoro, Apache-2.0). No good free Afrikaans voice exists, so the Afrikaans lines are read by the English voice using Afrikaans pronunciation rules; they can be swapped for a real voice later.
Only the chosen voice language is downloaded, after the first tap. Each voice pack is under 1 MB, and the first download is unchanged.
Share cards, the Daily share text and the end-of-hunt tally follow the text language.
feedback: Product owner (24 Oct): "I want options to have game and voice either German, English, Afrikaans. And text. Adjust also names accordingly, as the game needs to cater for multiple audiences."
Claude reviewed the names table before any files changed (German "Season Run" became "Saisonjagd").

The independent review found six things, all fixed before the merge: Oupa’s first greeting was usually silent because the voice was still loading, a test never proved a voice line was heard, a failed download was never retried, an old language’s voice stayed in memory, a stray build file was committed, and the setting hints were too small to read on phones.
On GitHub, a new voice test failed on the slow phone runner because it read Oupa’s line twice and the line had already gone. Claude fixed the test.

history.title: v1.6 Veld art: trees, fruit, far animals and the windmill
history.intro: The product owner wanted every map’s trees, bushes, grass and fruit at the quality of the camelthorn, and far animals that look like animals, not rough shapes.
bullets: Plants redrawn on every map at the camelthorn quality bar. Karoo: sweet thorns and aloes, renosterbos and ganna bushes. Bushveld: a baobab with hanging pods, mopane and marula with fallen fruit. Okavango: the sausage tree, jackalberries, ilala palms, papyrus and water lilies. Kalahari: shepherd’s trees, camelthorn pods and silvery Bushman grass. Namibië: quiver trees in yellow flower and !nara melons on the dunes.
Far animals redrawn with true body shapes: giraffes with real anatomy, patches and calves, springbok, gemsbok, zebra, wildebeest, elephants, lechwe and ostriches. They stay sharp through the scope.
Far trees are drawn per species with broken crowns, instead of blobs. Each area has realistic, softly drifting clouds of its own.
The dassie is bigger and more lifelike, on grey granite boulders. The dead camelthorn in the Kalahari is now a weathered tree skeleton.

The windmill was redrawn from the product owner’s photos: 20 curved sheet-metal sails, several missing, one bent and one torn, with rust. It turns into the wind and spins on windy days. The Kalahari windmill now has its wheel.

The placeholder-art bug is fixed: a hunt or the Skietbaan waits for its art behind a loading veil and retries if a file fails; the offline cache no longer serves an old file list after a new version goes live; a bar offers a reload when a new version is ready.
A build stamp on every map, the title and the Skietbaan: version, commit, date, area, weekday and whether the art loaded (for example "v1.6.0 · 89ec664 · 25 Oct 12:11 · Okavango · Sun · art ok").
A "Fresh load" button in the Skietbaan (test builds only) clears the game’s caches and reloads, without a manual hard refresh. The save is untouched.
The pale ring inside the scope is gone: it was the placeholder sight showing before the real one loaded.
Only the look changed: the game’s rules and replays are the same. First download 2.96 MB of 3 MB; every area pack within its 1.5 MB limit. 1 098 unit tests.
feedback: Product owner (25 Oct, about 06:50): the windmill needs more detail, a wheel with missing blades, and it should turn with the wind and spin.
About 07:00: the dassie "needs to be increased a lot". About 07:05: the giraffes’ "detail needs to become more realistic". About 07:10: the far trees look like blobs.
About 07:10–07:15: placeholder art on a MacBook Air in Brave, fixed by a hard reload. Claude traced it to the offline cache keeping an old file list after a deploy.
About 07:20: a version number on every map. About 07:25: the Kalahari dead tree "needs a lot of work" and the clouds "need to be more realistic".

Later, from the product owner’s photos of a real windmill: "not that ring on the outside … more missing ones, in random order … old and rusted". The redraw was approved: "looks great, implement it". The product owner also asked for the Fresh load button.

The independent review found five issues, all fixed: the reload bar showed when nothing had changed and sat over the game; a missing file list on the live site was not treated as an error; the scope and far-plane files that load late were not checked and retried; and parts of the view were not rebuilt once late art arrived.
Claude fixed the scope’s pale ring and the Kalahari windmill, whose wheel was hidden while the sign’s secret was live.
On GitHub, a loading test checked a retry counter too early (fixed); one long training-ground test timed out once on the slow runner and passed on a re-run.

history.title: v1.6b Reload power-ups: Blitslaai and Oupa Laai
history.intro: The product owner asked for "an AUTO reload, and a fast reload" as power-ups.
bullets: Blitslaai (Lightning Load): for 12 seconds every reload takes about a third of the time. It covers full-belt reloads, shell-by-shell reloads, the Voorlaaier’s ramrod and the Kettie’s draw. Small lightning glints hop along the rounds and a reload starts with a quick metallic zip.

Oupa Laai (Oupa Loads): for 12 seconds the gun reloads by itself the moment it is empty, and a shell-by-shell gun tops up when you pause. Oupa’s hand sits by the belt and he says "I’ll load for you, my kind!" (in English, Afrikaans and German). A shot always cuts an automatic reload, so it never locks you out of a shot.
Both come from supply crates in any hunt and cost 2 coins at the Padstal in a Season Run. They are the first power-ups with icons on their HUD chips.
Balance: the competent bot’s Classic score rose 1.9 %; every Season Run gate still passes (spring with good buys is 69.6 %, inside its target).
First download 3,026.6 KB of 3 MB (+13 KB for the icons, the glints, the zip and the code).
feedback: Main, with v1.6, was merged in as version 1.6.1. Claude changed one browser test so it always checks the lightning icon, not only sometimes.
A slow Skietbaan browser test (the D-040 gongs) timed out on GitHub, on main as well. Claude split it into two tests that shoot inside the page (#75), and the same fix went into this PR.
Screenshots of both power-ups on desktop and a phone were taken after the merge.

history.title: The Project overview page in the admin
history.intro: The product owner wanted one place to see the project’s status without asking: what is done and outstanding with dates and expected builds, open questions and decisions, what is built and what will be, suggestions, and the history with its pictures.
bullets: A "Project overview" button on the admin page (test builds only; players never download it).

Tabs: Overview (needs you, now building, up next, last done, numbers, links and recent activity), Roadmap (running, planned and done, each with its build number and expected time), Requests, Ideas, and History with pictures that open full size.
Every time is shown in Namibia time.
Claude updates the data on its own branch (project-log) at every merge and screenshot round, so the page is current within about 5 minutes, with no new build or deploy.
If the connection drops, the last copy that loaded is shown and marked as an offline copy.
Links and pictures are only accepted from the project’s own GitHub and Claude pages, so a crafted link can’t show a fake status.
Works on desktop, Pixel 7 and iPhone 14, with the page’s own text in English, Afrikaans, German and Dutch.
feedback: Claude’s own review moved "now building" to the top, put the roadmap in running → planned → done order, and kept lettered options (A, B, C) from being numbered twice.
The product owner looked before it was merged ("I don’t see the Project page"); it went live 25 minutes later.

history.title: v1.7 Meerkat colonies on the desert maps
history.intro: The product owner asked for meerkat holes on the desert maps, with meerkats that "peek out and run from one nest to the other. Be creative."
bullets: One or two meerkat colonies on every Kalahari and Namibië map, on burrow mounds with dark holes, fresh sand and tracks.

The meerkats peek, come out, sit, forage and sunbathe in Monday’s dawn light. A sentinel stands guard on the highest mound, and they dash between burrows in a file, stopping halfway to look. A pup follows its mother.

They react to the hunt: a shot nearby sends the colony down (the scout comes back first after 3–6 seconds); the Langloop sends every colony down; a raptor or the crop sprayer overhead sets off the sentinel’s alarm bark, which also alerts the nearest guineafowl flock.
Shooting a meerkat costs 10 points; it tumbles, then scolds you ("We’re not guineafowl!").

A new secret, the Familiefoto: hold fire for 4 seconds with a whole family out near the middle of the screen and they line up for a photo, with a camera click, for +25. It is in the Bird Book and has a Notaboek challenge.
They are part of the game’s rules, not decoration, so replays, challenge links and the Daily Hunt play them the same on every device.
Balance: on all 20 desert maps the scores stay within −1.2 % and +2.5 % of the same maps without colonies.
The meerkat art and sounds load with either desert map. A Kalahari hunt downloads 1,534.9 KB of its 1,536 KB limit; the first download is 3,055 KB.
feedback: Claude’s first look round: the meerkats looked flat, below the camelthorn quality bar. Redrawn with a rounded body, a cream belly, shading, an eye mask and a fluffier pup; the burrows got holes with shadows and fresh sand.
The independent review found a shot pup that stayed stuck for the rest of the hunt, and a placement check that ignored the mounds. Both fixed, with tests.
Colonies were moved so none sits under the HUD on desktop, Pixel 7 or iPhone 14, and so they stay clear of the gun. Meerkats now keep a body width apart.

Product owner (25 Oct, about 17:45): "a little bit more hairy … a tick more furry, and a little bit nicer faces". Round 3 drew every meerkat as fur, with a teardrop eye mask, a small eye with a catch-light and a short muzzle.

On GitHub, a browser test expected −10 for a meerkat shot but got +29: a bird near the moved colony shared the shot. The game was right; the test now takes a shot the meerkat gets alone. The balance was re-checked on all 20 maps after the move.

history.title: v1.7b Power-ups explained, and an Oupa switch
history.intro: The product owner: "When one collects these power-ups, one is very unsure what they actually do … there needs to be a clear indication in this menu", and an option to switch Oupa’s comments off because "some people would be irritated by always having a grandfather give his input".
bullets: Icons for all eight power-ups and crate guns, readable on a HUD chip and big in the Gun Shed.
A Power-ups tab in the Gun Shed: for each one a picture, one plain sentence of what it does with its numbers, how to get it, and a tip. Ones not found yet are marked, but still explained.

In the hunt: a falling crate shows the icon of what it holds, on the parachute and on the box; a card says what you picked up (the first time with Oupa’s word); the chip counts the seconds or shells down and blinks before it ends; each power-up has a small look of its own (an ∞ on the belt, a wider spread ring, a warm slow-motion tint); the tally lists the power-ups you used.

Settings → Oupa’s comments: On, Text only (his bubble without his voice) or Off. The tutorial and the first pickup still explain themselves as plain text when he is off; other voices (the meerkats, the weavers, the frog) still speak.
Every number the player reads comes from the content files; a test keeps hand-typed numbers out of the texts in all four languages.
The first download stayed under the 3 MB line (3,069 KB): the new icons load a little later in the hunt, before the first crate can drop.
feedback: Claude’s screenshots (desktop, Pixel 7, iPhone 14): the crate’s icon was too small and faint, the old floating item name still landed on the HUD, and two icons were too thin at chip size. All fixed and re-checked.

The independent review found the first download over 3 MB and the pickup card able to cover the crosshair, plus seven smaller points (a card in the training ground, a raw caption, Oupa’s switch silencing the meerkats, tests that could not fail, a changelog line, Oupa’s lines ignoring the Afrikaans names). All fixed.

Moving the icons to a later download caused a freeze right after a crate pickup on GitHub’s phone test: the placeholder icons were deleted while still on screen. Claude found it, fixed it (the placeholder is now renamed instead of deleted) and re-took all 45 screenshots before merging.

history.title: v1.7c Fruit that swings and drops
history.intro: The product owner, testing the sausage tree in the Okavango: "When shooting these fruits, make them swing or drop down."
bullets: Every hanging and tree fruit reacts to shots: the sausage tree’s sausages, baobab pods, marula, jackalberries, ilala clusters, sweet-thorn and camelthorn pods, quiver-tree flowers, and !nara melons on the ground.

A hit swings the fruit on its stalk; a near miss gives a smaller swing; a hard hit, or a second hit while it swings, snaps it off. It falls, bounces, rolls clear of the trunk and lies on the ground with a soft shadow. Small, local dust and leaf puffs; a soft thock and a thud.
Fruit are not targets: no score, no penalty, and the game’s rules and replays are unchanged. They take the map’s light of the day and its haze, like the trees they hang on.

All fruit redrawn as separate pictures at the camelthorn quality: heavy, mottled Kigelia sausages on rope stalks, velvety baobab pods, speckled marula. They load with their map, never in the first download.
feedback: Claude’s screenshots: the first fruit pictures were plain shapes (tan "pills", grey eggs), and a dropped sausage lay across the trunk. Redrawn at the camelthorn quality; dropped fruit now lands clear.

The independent review found that the fruit ignored the map’s light of the day and its haze, and that in wind a dead-centre shot could miss a fruit (the wind drift was applied twice); also fruit drawn over rocks and tree feet, work every frame, and steps on fast phones. All fixed.
Tank’s first session lost its connection before pushing; Claude retried it and no work was lost.

history.title: Halloween Spookjag (Feesdae)
history.intro: The product owner chose Halloween from the list of local Daily specials: "Halloween special yes, go ahead".
bullets: Special days (Feesdae): on a special day (by the UTC date) the Daily Hunt becomes that day’s special, the same for everyone. The special days live in the content files, so more holidays can be added later.
Halloween’s Spookjag (31 Oct, version 1.7.3): a dusk hunt with its own dark, cool light, under a big low moon with bats circling it.
Bats are fast bonus targets (+15). The spotted eagle-owl is protected: shooting one costs 10 points, and Oupa scolds you.

3–5 carved pumpkin lanterns stand on the tops of props (the reservoir rim, boulders, the bakkie’s roof) or on their own post. Each goes dark when shot. Putting them all out pays "Lanterns out! +25", once.
About a third of the guineafowl wear small witch hats.

The title’s Daily button reads Spookjag, with a "Spookjag tonight!" badge. The tally gets a Halloween frame, the title "Spookjag 2026" and a row for bats, owls and lanterns. The share text gets a Halloween frame too.
Sounds: an organ and kalimba sting, an owl hoot, a bat squeak and a lantern puff. Oupa has five Halloween lines in English, Afrikaans, German and Dutch, voiced in English, Afrikaans and German.
The Halloween pictures and sounds load in the background, only on the day. The first download stays under 3 MB (3,071 of 3,072 KB).

How to try it before 31 Oct on the public test build: the admin page → Special days → Spookjag · 31/10 → Play, then Play again on the next card. (The ?feesdag=halloween address only works on developer and test builds.)
feedback: The first independent review found that the hunt waited for all the Halloween files to download. It now starts as soon as the code is in; the pictures and sounds follow.

Claude’s review round, with screenshots on desktop and Pixel 7, listed 15 points, all fixed: scoring through the same path as every other bonus and penalty, an iPhone-safe Share tap and owl test, witch hats on the head in every frame, carved glowing lanterns placed where they read, a darker dusk, bigger owls on their own band below the HUD, overlaps on the title and the tally, Oupa’s lines loaded only when needed, a message if the Halloween files fail to load, and recorded test hunts (golden replays) that cover the bats, owls and lanterns.
Claude fixed the last overlap of the title badge and the tally test.
An iPhone test still expected the older replay format (replays now record the special day). Claude fixed it before merging.

history.title: Perspective: birds get smaller with distance
history.intro: The product owner, playing the Karoo: "the guineafowl, the further away they are, the smaller they get … the ostriches, because they’re far away, are small, but the guineafowl is even bigger than they are … still in such a way that one can still shoot them … this needs to apply to all the levels."
bullets: An audit first measured every far animal against the guineafowl. In the Karoo a far bird was about 12× too big beside the ostriches.
The distance planes got smaller: the middle from 0.5 to 0.42, the far from 0.22 to 0.15, the farthest from 0.1 to 0.07. A standing guineafowl is now 263, 110, 39 and 18 px tall from near to farthest.
The far herds are shown 3× bigger. The HD animal redraw will later draw them at their true sizes, with the ostriches about 2.7× taller again.
The Namibië waterhole animals were redrawn 5× taller in the same spots, standing head up.
Far birds keep a minimum hit size (18 px far, 10 px farthest), so they stay shootable. Only targets get it, never the birds you must not shoot. The Halloween bats and lanterns get it too.
Feathers, alarm bubbles, score pops and witch hats shrink with the birds.
The guineafowl pictures were redrawn at their new sizes. That made the first download 106 KB smaller (3,071 → 2,965 KB of 3,072).

Balance (500 hunts per test): every difficulty check that passed before still passes. Good players score about 1 % more; weaker players about 10 % less (accepted: smaller birds are what was asked). Shotguns score less on the far bonus maps, which are made for rifles. The Langloop was retuned to stay above its minimum.
Released as version 1.7.4, on every map.
feedback: The independent review found three things: the Halloween bats and lanterns had shrunk without the minimum hit size; the minimum hit size also widened the birds you must not shoot (now it is for targets only); and two difficulty checks failed in the first rough run. The first two were fixed before merging; the full 500-hunt run settled the checks.

Claude’s screenshots showed that the Karoo comparison had no far guineafowl beside the ostriches (the screenshot now uses Monday’s Verder, where a far flock forages by the ostriches), and that the Namibië waterhole animals were shapeless at their new size (redrawn standing head up).
One of Tank’s edits had deleted eleven older entries of the decision log. Tank restored them.

On the final test run two browser tests failed: the seeded test hunts’ shot patterns changed with the content, and the targets were smaller. Claude made both tests robust (more shots, no long waits, a lantern no flock stands in front of), and the full suite passed on all devices.

history.title: v1.8 Blikkies: tin cans on the fence posts
history.intro: The product owner asked for this on 24 Oct and again on 26 Oct: "On maps with fence posts, have some cans standing on them that can be shot off. They somersault when hit … The distance should vary … if you hit them again they continue spinning up and so on till you don’t see them anymore." And: "Faster, higher, more unpredictable."
bullets: A farm fence of 3–6 posts, with a tin can on each (a paint tin, a rusty can, a bean can and others), stands on 3–4 weekday maps of each farm area: the Karoo, the Bushveld, the Kalahari and Namibië. Depending on the day it stands near, in the middle or far away; the bonus maps push it further back.

Shoot a can and it somersaults off its post, away from the side you hit. Hit it again in the air and it kicks higher, spins faster and wobbles more. The 10th hit in the air always sends it out of the top of the screen: "Weg!" ("gone"). A can that lands lies in the grass for the rest of the hunt.
Cans are sized for their distance, like the birds. In the air the hit area is 2.5× the drawn can, so near cans are the easiest to juggle and far cans the hardest.

Points: knocking a can off 5, each hit in the air 8 plus 2 more each time, Weg! 15. Further cans pay more (near ×0.8, middle ×1.3, far ×2, Ver ×2.5). Only the Stampede multiplies them: a can shot neither breaks nor builds your Frenzy, and it does not count as a miss.

Chain pops on screen ("3× in the air!"), can sounds, Oupa’s lines, a Notaboek challenge and a new secret, the Blikkiesdans (8 hits in the air, once a hunt). The Skietbaan has a Tin Cans target at every distance. Cans are not in the Season Run or the tutorial.

A new balance bot that shoots a flying can at the top of its arc measured the juggle over 500 hunts per test: a good shot gets 3 or more hits in the air on 98 % of near cans, 47 % of middle cans and none far away. Cans never make up more than 8.7 % of a score, and every difficulty check passes.
The can art is one small 14.9 KB sheet. The first download grew by 22 KB, to 2,987 of 3,072 KB.
Released as version 1.8.0.
feedback: The independent review found that far cans could be juggled almost forever (a computer shooter kept them up for 16–19 hits, worth more than a whole hunt of birds), and that on the near fence a chain of three was rare because the second hit already threw the can off the top. Tank capped the chain at 10 hits (always ending in Weg!), dropped the minimum hit size for cans in the air, softened the kicks and the sideways drift, and added the apex-juggler bot to prove it.
The review also found that new Skietbaan cans could stand on invisible posts after the view panned. The fence is now rebuilt whenever its posts move.

Claude’s first juggle screenshots reached only two hits, on the middle fence, where the can was tiny. The screenshot now juggles on the near fence and holds the frame while "3× in the air!" is on screen.

The new content changed the seeded test hunts, which broke two Halloween browser tests (the owls, and a lantern at the edge of the map). Claude fixed both on main (#85, #86) before the merge, and the full suite passed on all devices.
Tank’s connection to its model dropped several times during this job, so Claude restarted it as a fresh task with a self-contained brief, as the product owner had asked.
